why: policy.js and settings.js are byte-identical COPIES of the BGOS agent-browser rule tier, so a daemon-placed agent is judged by exactly the rules the desktop Agent Browser uses. A second copy of a permission policy is how two hosts quietly come to disagree about what is sensitive; the sha256 below is what makes the copy checkable instead of merely claimed.
whyADirectory: settings.js does require("./policy"), so the copies keep their ORIGINAL filenames and sit together. package.json here pins type=commonjs, because the plugin root declares type=module and these two files are CommonJS.
howToUpdate: Re-copy both from the BGOS paths above, rerun the hashes, update this file, and run: HOAI_BROWSER_HOST_CORE_SOURCE=<BGOS agent-browser dir> npx tsx --test test/browser-host-core.vendor.test.ts
theHalfThisCannotSee: Nothing here fires when the BGOS originals change and these copies do not. That check lives on the BGOS side in frontend/electron-app/agent-browser/__tests__/hostCoreVendorPin.test.js, which pins the same two hashes.
